subject.title: [Feature]: Standardize skill data directory convention (configPaths) under ~/.openclaw/

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class per-skill writable data contract, and if so should it be a filesystem convention, plugin/skill state API, or ClawHub authoring rule?
rationale: The current code has package and tool roots, but choosing runtime state storage affects public skill metadata, storage policy, security review, docs, and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Design first-class skill storage
options.body: Add a generic, documented storage contract with clear ownership, security semantics, tests, and docs before exposing new metadata or placeholders.

options.title: Publish ClawHub guidance only
options.body: Keep core behavior unchanged and document a ClawHub authoring convention for skills that need files, accepting that OpenClaw will not create or resolve a data root.

options.title: Decline new storage surface
options.body: Keep using existing skill package roots, `{baseDir}`, and installer `tools` paths, and close the request as not planned after maintainer confirmation.

recommendation.title: Design first-class skill storage
recommendation.body: Add a generic, documented storage contract with clear ownership, security semantics, tests, and docs before exposing new metadata or placeholders.

likelyOwner.reason: The closest available history points to repeated work on skill install, metadata, and docs surfaces that this decision would change.
